La película empieza poderosa, en medio de la tempestad, un hombre con su caballo intentando que el viento no se los lleve, una música ensordecedora y te meten una cita de Nietzsche en una transición igual de magnífica que el comienzo. Esos son los primeros cinco minutos de película, parecía pometedor y luego ves al hombre entrando en su rutina, se mete a casa y... empiezan a comer papas. Toda la película es un hombre levantándose de la cama, comiendo papas y volviéndose a acostar. Hay un trecho enorme de la película donde el hombre solo se la pasa comiéndose unas malditas papas. No pasa nada, no pasa más nada. Bien, me quieres vender la cotidianidad, pero, ¿me tenías que hacerme tragar la rutina de varios días del mismo hombre comiéndose unas papas? Más o menos a mitad de película llega un sujeto a la casa y dije: finalmente se dignaron a que pasara algo. Pero no, el sujeto era una herramienta al espectador para darnos contexto de toda la situación, pero la actuación es pobre y es una inmediata verborrea con toques líricos y poco destellos narrativos. Ahí dije: suficiente. No pude seguir viendo más, sé que pasa algo al final, pero no importa. Creo que estamos acostumbrados a que pase algo, sé que el director es así, la otra vez hizo tragarme 15 minutos de una persona caminando, pero la película duraba sus seis horas, quince minutos eran un pestañeo, pero aquí... esa grandilocuencia del inicio no se concreta con el hombre comiendo papas y menos con ese final que pareciera más el empate del inicio. Perfectamente la película se pudo haber terminado con el hombre comiendo papas y hubiese sido la misma basura. Decepcionante, aburrida y muy pobremente escrita. Que no se me malentienda, amo el cine somnífero, pero hay límites que simplemente no se pueden cruzar.

I dip into slow cinema once every six months to challenge myself by going out of my comfort zone but this is my last detour in my journey to watch all of film canon. A father and daughter survive a storm which could be interesting if it was an hour shorter. There are only so many ways you could show a man peeling a potato before you send the audience running back to their phones. More than the slow pace I am bothered by the lack of narrative. I have mentioned in other reviews – The decision to let the visuals do the heavy lifting does not work for me in spite of some beautiful, painterly images. Cinema is not just a visual medium it is a visual storytelling medium. That is not a difference in semantics but in function. The slow pace is an invitation to think but the movie does not give me much food for thought. Arthouse films peaked in the 60s with the likes of Fellini, Bergman, Antonioni and Rohmer. All of them are on the slower side but they ask incisive questions about sex, religion and creativity. They reward thinking you have to ponder about the character motivation to get most out of them. On the other hand slow cinema from directors like Tarr, Claire Denis or Abbas Kiarostami has one-note characters who never give the impression of having rich inner lives so thinking about them adds nothing to the experience. They are just badly paced, thematically empty and unabashedly self-indulgent. I am not fond of either extremes – I hate both Fast and Furious and its ilk, and slow cinema. Neither has any semblance of story and to enjoy them one has to either stop thinking or give into overthinking.

Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "positivas" (3.5–5 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews positivas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

Formato de saída (JSON puro):

[1] nota=3.5 estrelas:
Inception is a film made for the big screen. I remember it being exciting, new and so much fun on first viewing, so awe inspiring in theatres.  The movie falter a bit on repeat viewing, (there’s an emptiness that peaks its head out every once in a while), but it does hold up. I love that Christopher Nolan just decided to retro-fit this sci-fi story onto a heist narrative.  It works well! The team assembles, they all get their moments to shine, and they scatter with a knowing nod at the end of the robbery. This film has a LOT of things going on, it really walks a tightrope without managing to fall onto the hard pavement, although there are some close calls.  As is normal with a Nolan film, it’s too long. I think some of that could have been dealt with in the editing, but I’m not entirely sure what I would cut. It’s not really a detriment to the film, but why does Nolan insist on weird names like Ariatne? I get that there’s a literary reference there, but it’s a hard word for half the cast to say comfortably. But that ending is a corker! The spinning top.  The great musical swell by Hans Zimmer.

[6] nota=4.0 estrelas:
I slept on Inception, no pun intended, for quite a while before finally checking it out.  I was aware of the metaphor for filmmaking and such and some complaints that for a world set in dreams, it's rather unambitious in dealing with the unreal.  And while I'm sure more could have been done to make something more challenging and experimental, the film as is acts as a fantastic ride while being a metaphor for being Christopher Nolan, a man whose work probably keeps him from his kids. But I think part of the reason I forgive the lack of being overtly fantastical in the way that a Nightmare on Elm Street might be is that because it is about filmmaking, it is a fun heist movie exploring the idea of using the pieces and ideas a viewer already knows and how when properly utilized can be a way to bring in a new idea to the viewer.  If anything, I feel this is not what Nolan thinks he does specifically but also aspirational, in hopes of being the man who can put in a new idea.  And like a thief it needs to be done with tact so eventually the "target" and become a part of the same side, with your defenses overcome in the face of an idea baked in emotion. But if this was all "idea" it wouldn't work.  The way it works is that Nolan is a tactful and even fun filmmaker, even if the films aren't big on laughs.  It's easy to think of Nolan as a maker of blockbusters that feel more "dour" but he is actually an expert ride-crafter where the goal is to make a blockbuster that still wants to explore ideas but are also a blast to watch.

Rewatched Inception to put my thoughts in which film I thought was better- Paprika or this. Getting the record straight: Inception, despite being an exposition-heavy/slow paced film, is better overall in comparison to Paprika. My opinion why is this: First off, Inception has that sort of style in which everything is difficult, yet fairly easy to understand. It may be slow, but there are multiple visually pleasing scenes/intense action sequences that keep the audience in put, also with more actually innovative narrative that just begged to be seen. Second, paprika? One can’t deny the possible influence it had on Inception, but you also can’t deny the fact that Paprika relied more heavily on a style-over-substance approach and “dream logic” to patch up its obviously weak narrative. Many that love Paprika usually trash Inception without ever knowing that Inception at least has something to hold bound to instead of what’s basically a art-showcase. There’s too much going on to even care, especially when Paprika is already slow as hell. In a simple summary, Inception may have copied Paprika- we’ll never know, but it surely became superior to it and told a much more engrossing story than Paprika will ever be. 8/10.

Desde el principio presenta una idea muy original: entrar en los sueños de otras personas para obtener o implantar información (como es el caso en esta película). Es un concepto complejo, pero la película logra desarrollarlo de una forma que se vuelve cada vez más interesante conforme avanza la historia. Lo que más me gustó fue precisamente el concepto de los sueños, las actuaciones y los giros de trama. La forma en que Nolan construye distintos niveles de sueños y hace que todos funcionen al mismo tiempo es algo que pocas películas han intentado hacer. Leonardo DiCaprio hace una gran actuación como Cobb. Además de liderar al equipo, consigue transmitir el peso emocional que carga durante toda la historia. También me gustó mucho la dinámica que tiene con los demás miembros del grupo, ya que hace que la misión se sienta más real y que te intereses por lo que les ocurre a todos. Mi escena favorita fue la batalla final. Es un momento lleno de tensión, acción y emoción donde todas las piezas de la historia comienzan a encajar. Además, la forma en que se conectan los diferentes niveles de sueños hace que la secuencia sea aún más emocionante. La música es otro de los puntos fuertes de la película. Ayuda a crear una sensación constante de misterio, urgencia y grandeza que encaja perfectamente con la historia. Algo que también me parece destacable es el uso de efectos prácticos. Nolan evitó depender completamente del CGI y utilizó escenarios reales, efectos físicos y cámaras IMAX para muchas secuencias importantes. Esto hace que escenas como los pasillos giratorios o los cambios de gravedad se sigan viendo espectaculares incluso años después de su estreno. Una película inteligente, emocionante y visualmente espectacular que demuestra por qué Christopher Nolan es uno de los directores más importantes.

Inception is a film made for the big screen. I remember it being exciting, new and so much fun on first viewing, so awe inspiring in theatres.  The movie falter a bit on repeat viewing, (there’s an emptiness that peaks its head out every once in a while), but it does hold up. I love that Christopher Nolan just decided to retro-fit this sci-fi story onto a heist narrative.  It works well! The team assembles, they all get their moments to shine, and they scatter with a knowing nod at the end of the robbery. This film has a LOT of things going on, it really walks a tightrope without managing to fall onto the hard pavement, although there are some close calls.  As is normal with a Nolan film, it’s too long. I think some of that could have been dealt with in the editing, but I’m not entirely sure what I would cut. It’s not really a detriment to the film, but why does Nolan insist on weird names like Ariatne? I get that there’s a literary reference there, but it’s a hard word for half the cast to say comfortably. But that ending is a corker! The spinning top.  The great musical swell by Hans Zimmer.

I slept on Inception, no pun intended, for quite a while before finally checking it out.  I was aware of the metaphor for filmmaking and such and some complaints that for a world set in dreams, it's rather unambitious in dealing with the unreal.  And while I'm sure more could have been done to make something more challenging and experimental, the film as is acts as a fantastic ride while being a metaphor for being Christopher Nolan, a man whose work probably keeps him from his kids. But I think part of the reason I forgive the lack of being overtly fantastical in the way that a Nightmare on Elm Street might be is that because it is about filmmaking, it is a fun heist movie exploring the idea of using the pieces and ideas a viewer already knows and how when properly utilized can be a way to bring in a new idea to the viewer.  If anything, I feel this is not what Nolan thinks he does specifically but also aspirational, in hopes of being the man who can put in a new idea.  And like a thief it needs to be done with tact so eventually the "target" and become a part of the same side, with your defenses overcome in the face of an idea baked in emotion. But if this was all "idea" it wouldn't work.  The way it works is that Nolan is a tactful and even fun filmmaker, even if the films aren't big on laughs.  It's easy to think of Nolan as a maker of blockbusters that feel more "dour" but he is actually an expert ride-crafter where the goal is to make a blockbuster that still wants to explore ideas but are also a blast to watch.

Rewatched Inception to put my thoughts in which film I thought was better- Paprika or this. Getting the record straight: Inception, despite being an exposition-heavy/slow paced film, is better overall in comparison to Paprika. My opinion why is this: First off, Inception has that sort of style in which everything is difficult, yet fairly easy to understand. It may be slow, but there are multiple visually pleasing scenes/intense action sequences that keep the audience in put, also with more actually innovative narrative that just begged to be seen. Second, paprika? One can’t deny the possible influence it had on Inception, but you also can’t deny the fact that Paprika relied more heavily on a style-over-substance approach and “dream logic” to patch up its obviously weak narrative. Many that love Paprika usually trash Inception without ever knowing that Inception at least has something to hold bound to instead of what’s basically a art-showcase. There’s too much going on to even care, especially when Paprika is already slow as hell. In a simple summary, Inception may have copied Paprika- we’ll never know, but it surely became superior to it and told a much more engrossing story than Paprika will ever be. 8/10.

Desde el principio presenta una idea muy original: entrar en los sueños de otras personas para obtener o implantar información (como es el caso en esta película). Es un concepto complejo, pero la película logra desarrollarlo de una forma que se vuelve cada vez más interesante conforme avanza la historia. Lo que más me gustó fue precisamente el concepto de los sueños, las actuaciones y los giros de trama. La forma en que Nolan construye distintos niveles de sueños y hace que todos funcionen al mismo tiempo es algo que pocas películas han intentado hacer. Leonardo DiCaprio hace una gran actuación como Cobb. Además de liderar al equipo, consigue transmitir el peso emocional que carga durante toda la historia. También me gustó mucho la dinámica que tiene con los demás miembros del grupo, ya que hace que la misión se sienta más real y que te intereses por lo que les ocurre a todos. Mi escena favorita fue la batalla final. Es un momento lleno de tensión, acción y emoción donde todas las piezas de la historia comienzan a encajar. Además, la forma en que se conectan los diferentes niveles de sueños hace que la secuencia sea aún más emocionante. La música es otro de los puntos fuertes de la película. Ayuda a crear una sensación constante de misterio, urgencia y grandeza que encaja perfectamente con la historia. Algo que también me parece destacable es el uso de efectos prácticos. Nolan evitó depender completamente del CGI y utilizó escenarios reales, efectos físicos y cámaras IMAX para muchas secuencias importantes. Esto hace que escenas como los pasillos giratorios o los cambios de gravedad se sigan viendo espectaculares incluso años después de su estreno. Una película inteligente, emocionante y visualmente espectacular que demuestra por qué Christopher Nolan es uno de los directores más importantes.

Дети: В воспоминаниях и снах Кобб никогда не видит лиц своих детей, и они всегда одеты одинаково. В финале они наконец оборачиваются, а в титрах указаны другие актеры, так как дети подросли. Сам Кристофер Нолан на Variety отмечал, что интеллектуально Кобб находится в реальности, но эмоционально ему уже всё равно. Он уходит к детям, даже не дожидаясь, упадет ли волчок. Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "negativas" (0.5–2 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews negativas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

I was honestly surprised when I went back to Letterboxd and saw that this was a 4.4. It’s far off that for me. I know I started watching this when I was younger and stopped it. At the time, I think it was just for the gore, but maybe it was also me already knowing that I wasn’t going to like what the movie was. Also, clearly, my parents had absolutely no control over what I watched. But anyway. There were a few things I liked: Christoph Waltz’s performance, the colour choices, and… that’s pretty much it. I really didn’t like the pacing. There were so many scenes that felt unnecessarily prolonged and, to me, added very little to the story. And there are so many storylines that felt unfinished or underdeveloped. Honestly, I would have found the story of how the propaganda machine worked, how they turned Zoller into this heroic figure, made a movie about him, and used cinema as propaganda, so much more interesting. Or even Shosanna’s story: how she got the cinema, how she planned her revenge, and what she was actually trying to achieve. There was so much potential in both of these storylines. Instead, Zoller’s storyline becomes this weird thing where he seems almost harmless, even though he killed 300 enemies, randomly falls in love with Shosanna, and then, in the final moments, you actually see who he really is. I just kept thinking there was so much more that could have been done with these characters and their stories. And then, of course, the bane of my existence in movies: American soldiers coming to save the world. I’ve always hated that concept and I will always hate that concept. Apart from that, one of the things that annoyed me the most was how much time is spent building Hans Landa up as this terrifying and intelligent character, only for his story to end the way it does. He’s obviously a horrible character, but after all that build-up, I expected a much more ba-bam ending. Shout-out to Christoph Waltz, though. He was the main reason I kept watching, so naturally I was even more annoyed by how his character ended. And probably the biggest problem for me is that the movie felt childish at times, especially when it was trying to be funny. A situation like this is not funny to me, and some of the comedy completely took me out of it. The buongiorno scene that everyone seems to love, apparently peak comedy? I was just sitting there thinking, really? And cringing so much. Even the music, which I thought could have saved the movie a little bit for me, sometimes felt wasted. There were moments where I felt like it wasn’t being used at the right time, and some of the tension could have been so much better. Something about the pacing, the music, or simply the way the scenes were handled just didn’t get me there. The movie felt like it was lacking so much of its potential, and I think that was most obvious during those scenes. Maybe I’m missing something, but for a movie that is so highly rated and so highly praised, I spent a lot of it thinking: this is it?

[11] nota=1.5 estrelas:
BASTARDOS INGLÓRIOS Extremamente fraco, mal dirigido e, para mim, um filme ruim e até desrespeitoso. O maior problema é a maneira como Bastardos Inglórios trata a Segunda Guerra Mundial. A guerra e o horror nazista são transformados em uma espécie de fantasia estilizada, quase como se tudo tivesse sido construído para ser divertido e satisfatório. Para mim, isso tira muito do peso do período que está sendo retratado. E o humor também não funciona. É um filme para maiores de 18 anos, mas em vários momentos parece ter sido escrito para adolescentes que acham violência e palavrão automaticamente engraçados. Algumas cenas parecem existir apenas para virar uma edit no TikTok. A única coisa que realmente consigo elogiar é Christoph Waltz. Hans Landa é disparado a melhor parte do filme, e Waltz entende perfeitamente o personagem. Ele consegue fazer o sujeito ser carismático sem deixar de ser repulsivo, e sua atuação realmente merece todos os elogios que recebeu. Fora isso, não consegui encontrar muita coisa que me interessasse. Os personagens são pouco envolventes, o roteiro se apoia demais no estilo e eu pessoalmente não gosto da maneira como Tarantino dirige seus filmes. Violência estilizada e aquela necessidade constante de transformar tudo em uma cena “icônica” simplesmente não funcionam comigo. Talvez eu seja uma das poucas pessoas que realmente não entende todo esse amor pelo filme. Para mim, Bastardos Inglórios parece muito mais interessado em ser cool do que em dizer alguma coisa sobre a guerra que está retratando. -P.F. Prado

I was honestly surprised when I went back to Letterboxd and saw that this was a 4.4. It’s far off that for me. I know I started watching this when I was younger and stopped it. At the time, I think it was just for the gore, but maybe it was also me already knowing that I wasn’t going to like what the movie was. Also, clearly, my parents had absolutely no control over what I watched. But anyway. There were a few things I liked: Christoph Waltz’s performance, the colour choices, and… that’s pretty much it. I really didn’t like the pacing. There were so many scenes that felt unnecessarily prolonged and, to me, added very little to the story. And there are so many storylines that felt unfinished or underdeveloped. Honestly, I would have found the story of how the propaganda machine worked, how they turned Zoller into this heroic figure, made a movie about him, and used cinema as propaganda, so much more interesting. Or even Shosanna’s story: how she got the cinema, how she planned her revenge, and what she was actually trying to achieve. There was so much potential in both of these storylines. Instead, Zoller’s storyline becomes this weird thing where he seems almost harmless, even though he killed 300 enemies, randomly falls in love with Shosanna, and then, in the final moments, you actually see who he really is. I just kept thinking there was so much more that could have been done with these characters and their stories. And then, of course, the bane of my existence in movies: American soldiers coming to save the world. I’ve always hated that concept and I will always hate that concept. Apart from that, one of the things that annoyed me the most was how much time is spent building Hans Landa up as this terrifying and intelligent character, only for his story to end the way it does. He’s obviously a horrible character, but after all that build-up, I expected a much more ba-bam ending. Shout-out to Christoph Waltz, though. He was the main reason I kept watching, so naturally I was even more annoyed by how his character ended. And probably the biggest problem for me is that the movie felt childish at times, especially when it was trying to be funny. A situation like this is not funny to me, and some of the comedy completely took me out of it. The buongiorno scene that everyone seems to love, apparently peak comedy? I was just sitting there thinking, really? And cringing so much. Even the music, which I thought could have saved the movie a little bit for me, sometimes felt wasted. There were moments where I felt like it wasn’t being used at the right time, and some of the tension could have been so much better. Something about the pacing, the music, or simply the way the scenes were handled just didn’t get me there. The movie felt like it was lacking so much of its potential, and I think that was most obvious during those scenes. Maybe I’m missing something, but for a movie that is so highly rated and so highly praised, I spent a lot of it thinking: this is it?

BASTARDOS INGLÓRIOS Extremamente fraco, mal dirigido e, para mim, um filme ruim e até desrespeitoso. O maior problema é a maneira como Bastardos Inglórios trata a Segunda Guerra Mundial. A guerra e o horror nazista são transformados em uma espécie de fantasia estilizada, quase como se tudo tivesse sido construído para ser divertido e satisfatório. Para mim, isso tira muito do peso do período que está sendo retratado. E o humor também não funciona. É um filme para maiores de 18 anos, mas em vários momentos parece ter sido escrito para adolescentes que acham violência e palavrão automaticamente engraçados. Algumas cenas parecem existir apenas para virar uma edit no TikTok. A única coisa que realmente consigo elogiar é Christoph Waltz. Hans Landa é disparado a melhor parte do filme, e Waltz entende perfeitamente o personagem. Ele consegue fazer o sujeito ser carismático sem deixar de ser repulsivo, e sua atuação realmente merece todos os elogios que recebeu. Fora isso, não consegui encontrar muita coisa que me interessasse. Os personagens são pouco envolventes, o roteiro se apoia demais no estilo e eu pessoalmente não gosto da maneira como Tarantino dirige seus filmes. Violência estilizada e aquela necessidade constante de transformar tudo em uma cena “icônica” simplesmente não funcionam comigo. Talvez eu seja uma das poucas pessoas que realmente não entende todo esse amor pelo filme. Para mim, Bastardos Inglórios parece muito mais interessado em ser cool do que em dizer alguma coisa sobre a guerra que está retratando. -P.F. Prado

Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "positivas" (3.5–5 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews positivas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.

4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.

[19] nota=4.5 estrelas:
When first watching Memories of Murder: I had heard that it was a masterpiece of True Crime filmmaking. I had watched many Korean horror films but this was the first drama/true crime foreign film. I'll admit, I didn't really get it the first time. All the detectives are kind of inept and do some pretty bad things themselves. So who do we route for? And that ending .... What!? But for years it stuck with me. So I started looking into it and realized "Oh, this was based on an actual serial killing in South Korea." And not just a serial killing, but what many would consider to be the first modern serial killer in South Korea. The director, Bong Joon-ho, probably remembered and experienced some of this growing up.  The police were actually pretty inept did infact torture confessions from people and were in over their heads. While creative liberties were taken, timelines shortened and some people involved changes: the telling is quite accurate. Knowing that now, Memories of Murder becomes much more engaging, interesting and poignant. All of our characters are shades of grey because the detectives were in fact torturing confessions from people, were incredibly under resources and frequently went off of feelings or hunches because of a lack of evidence. While being culturallydifferent from traditional American detective stories (Zodiac and Seven come to mind) once you get used to the Korean style and culture, with some added understanding of the true events that inspire the story, Memories of Murder really is a master piece in true crime filmmaking. It is also an interesting look at a director's early work that would carry them into greater future success.

When first watching Memories of Murder: I had heard that it was a masterpiece of True Crime filmmaking. I had watched many Korean horror films but this was the first drama/true crime foreign film. I'll admit, I didn't really get it the first time. All the detectives are kind of inept and do some pretty bad things themselves. So who do we route for? And that ending .... What!? But for years it stuck with me. So I started looking into it and realized "Oh, this was based on an actual serial killing in South Korea." And not just a serial killing, but what many would consider to be the first modern serial killer in South Korea. The director, Bong Joon-ho, probably remembered and experienced some of this growing up.  The police were actually pretty inept did infact torture confessions from people and were in over their heads. While creative liberties were taken, timelines shortened and some people involved changes: the telling is quite accurate. Knowing that now, Memories of Murder becomes much more engaging, interesting and poignant. All of our characters are shades of grey because the detectives were in fact torturing confessions from people, were incredibly under resources and frequently went off of feelings or hunches because of a lack of evidence. While being culturallydifferent from traditional American detective stories (Zodiac and Seven come to mind) once you get used to the Korean style and culture, with some added understanding of the true events that inspire the story, Memories of Murder really is a master piece in true crime filmmaking. It is also an interesting look at a director's early work that would carry them into greater future success.

Gerade geguckt: „Memories of Murder“ ist ein Kriminal Thriller welcher 1986, in einer kleinen Provinz, im von der Militärdiktatur geprägten Südkorea spielt. Es geht um zwei ungleiche Kommissarre, die versuchen eine Reihe von Morden aufzuklären, welche immer an einem verregneten Tag und an rot gekleideten Frauen begangen werden. Allerdings ist der Film nicht nur ein einfacher Krimi sondern auch eine Nachricht an den echten Mörder, welcher erst 16 Jahre nach dem erscheinen des Films gefasst wurde. Abgesehen davon Thematisiert der Film die Inkompetenz der Polizei und den moralischen Verfall einer der Kommissare sowie Südkorea im Chaos des kurz bevorstehenden Umbruchs der Diktatur. Regisseur Bong Joon-ho zeichnet mit „Memorie of Murder“ ein atmosphärisches und immer düsterer werdendes Portrait einer traumatisierten Gesellschaft in wunderschönen aber dreckigen Bildern. Die letzte Szene ging mit einem einfachen aber tief gehenden Blick in die Kamera, nicht zu Unrecht in die Filmgeschichte ein. „Memories of Murder“ wird mir wahrscheinlich noch die nächsten Tage im Gedächtnis bleiben und motiviert mich weiter in Bong Joon-ho‘s Vita und das Koreanische Kino einzutauchen. Meiner Meinung nach einer der besten Filme seines Genres, die ich bis jetzt gesehen habe. Kann ich jedem empfehlen. (Btw noch nie so viele Dropkicks in einem ernsten Film gesehen)
